summary: This This Old House segment guides a homeowner through safely replacing an aged ceiling fixture in a house built in 1960. The hosts inspect the new LED fixture for pre-1985 wiring compatibility, demonstrate turning off power at the panel, and address the risks of using outdated cloth NM cable with low temperature ratings. To accommodate modern fixtures, they splice in new wiring and install a new metal junction box in the ceiling, routing conductors through an attic/crawl-space path, bonding the ground, and reassembling the fixture with LED bulbs. The episode emphasizes heat management near junction boxes, explains the 60°C versus 90°C insulation jacket ratings, and demonstrates how to identify cable types (NM, NM-B) and what labeling signifies for safe installation.

sections.title: Fixture evaluation and safety warning
concepts: initial assessment of wiring in a 1960-built house
sections.description: Heath and Brette introduce the project: a homeowner has bought a new fixture with a warning about wiring in houses built before 1985, and they plan to inspect the current wiring before installation.

sections.title: Wiring assessment and planning
concepts: risk of heat and brittle insulation
sections.description: They examine the existing junction box wiring (cloth-covered NM cable, 60°C rated) and explain why incandescent-era installations could overheat. They describe the code change in the early 1980s to require higher temperature-rated insulation (90°C) and discuss LED bulbs as a lower-heat option, while noting the socket type still accepts common bulbs.

sections.title: Wiring extension and box installation
sections.description: Because the old wires do not line up with a single junction box, the team routes wires through an attic/crawl-space path, installs a new ceiling junction box, strips the jacket, feeds the wire through a connector, and bonds the ground to prepare for the new fixture.

sections.title: Fixture installation and testing
concepts: heat considerations near the junction box
sections.description: The new fixture is mounted, LED bulbs and glass are installed, and the power is restored to verify operation. The hosts discuss the importance of spacing the heat source away from the junction box and recap safety considerations.

featured_techniques.technique: Extending wiring and installing a new ceiling junction box to support a modern fixture

Routing wiring through attic/crawl spaces to reach a new junction box
Cable identification and code-history explanation: distinguishing NM, NM-B, and jacket ratings (60°C vs 90°C)
